messages:
Nadia: quick sync: legal wants a clear guarantee that EU-resident tenant writes never leave the EU. can we support active/active without sync cross-region writes?

Ravi: short: yes, with local-first + replication, but we must enforce a hard routing block and strong telemetry. otherwise attempts are a compliance risk.

Parker: two modes matter here: resident-only (no cross-region attempts ever) and geo-accelerated (writes can be forwarded). resident-only gives best compliance. geo-accelerated gives latency but needs explicit consent.

Lena: operational concerns: if we block attempts at the proxy level, make sure error code is distinct (e.g., 451) and logged with tenant id + origin region. infra-bot can emit an audit event.

infra-bot: audit rule created: residency.write_block -> emits events to `audit-residency` stream.

Marta: data plane design: route writes for resident-only tenants to resident region queue; local region can accept read-cache only. replication is async with per-tenant priority. we should tag each replica with `origin_region` + `origin_ts`.

Ravi: agree on tags. add `replication_policy` per tenant: `immediate`, `batch`, `low_priority`. default for regulated tenants = `immediate` but still async.

Parker: how do clients see freshness? propose header: `X-Residency-Freshness: fresh|lag=120ms`. also offer param `force_resident=true` to do a resident synchronous read if they need linearizability (expensive).

Lena: also need cache behaviour: local caches should have adaptive TTLs. suggestion: default read cache 20s, session cache 5s, but when resident region latency spikes, increase local TTL to 1m to prevent overload. document circuit-breaker thresholds.

Nadia: legal note: even attempted cross-region writes could be considered export in some regions. so proxies must deny at the edge and never queue outbound cross-region write attempts for resident-only tenants.

Ravi: implementation detail: proxy consults control-plane for tenant residency at auth time and adds `X-Tenant-Residency` header. reject early with 451 if mismatch. cache residency decision for 60s in proxy.

infra-bot: created feature flag `residency-v2-proxy-checks` for canary rollout.

Marta: replication considerations: keep an append-only commit log per-tenant in resident region. replicas pull, apply idempotently. ensure replay window and tombstone TTL.

Theo: KMS implication: resident-only tenants should use region-bound CMKs. cross-region replicas must store wrapped keys and never unwrap outside origin region. Luis (security) to confirm.

Parker: monitoring: emit `attempted_nonresident_write`, `blocked_nonresident_write`, `replication_lag_ms`, `stale_read_rate` per-tenant. set alert if blocked events > 0 for a new tenant rollout (might indicate misconfigured client).

Ravi: chaos test plan: simulate resident-region outage and verify control-plane flips allowed behaviour: by default keep resident-only blocked, but ops can temporarily mark tenant as `emergency-permissive` with explicit audit and legal ok. add TTL to emergency flags.

Nadia: decision: resident-only mode = default for regulated tenants; proxies must reject nonresident writes with 451; async replication allowed but keys and audit must remain resident-bound. permissive/accelerated mode available only with customer opt-in.

Lena: action items: @Ravi add proxy header + 451 response, @Marta design per-tenant commit log + replication tags, @Theo confirm KMS constraints with security, @Parker add freshness headers + force param, @infra-bot roll canary flag.

Nadia: thanks — I'll draft the RFC follow-up with the snippets and a compact runbook (canary size, metrics, chaos test steps). planning to open RFC PR today.

Marta: FYI I dropped a starter test matrix under docs/arch/multi-region-residency/ for reviewers.

Theo: will ping security for KMS review.

Ravi: +1, will start proxy patching this afternoon.

Nadia: awesome. closing thread, will link RFC once PR is up.
